articles.summary: Carrier screening asks whether a future child could inherit a known condition. Reproductive-gene screening asks whether a pregnancy can develop at all. They overlap far less than most people expect.
articles.title: Reproductive Gene Screening vs. Carrier Screening: Why They're Not the Same Test

articles.summary: PADI6 is part of the machinery an egg loads in advance to switch on an embryo's own genome. When both copies are altered, embryos can arrest in the first few days. Here is what that means in plain language.
articles.title: PADI6 and Early Embryo Arrest: A Maternal-Effect Gene Explained

articles.summary: NLRP7 is the main gene behind recurrent molar pregnancy, a maternal-effect condition that can repeat across pregnancies and partners. Here is what it does, why it recurs, and what testing can clarify.
articles.title: NLRP7, Molar Pregnancy, and Recurrent Loss: What the Gene Explains

articles.summary: TUBB8, NLRP7, PADI6, NLRP5 and their relatives act in the egg to run the first days of development. Variants can cause embryo arrest and recurrent loss that chromosome tests miss. Here is the plain-language map.
articles.title: Maternal-Effect Genes: The Pregnancy-Loss Genes a Karyotype Can't See

articles.summary: TUBB8 builds the spindle that lets an egg divide. When it is altered, eggs can stall before they mature or embryos can arrest early. Here is what the gene does, how it is inherited, and what testing can and cannot tell you.
articles.title: TUBB8: The Gene Behind Some Cases of Egg and Embryo Arrest

articles.summary: A plain-language look at Reticular's parent-only reproductive-gene screen: what it covers, the research it draws on, what a result can and cannot mean, and where it fits alongside standard testing.
articles.title: The Reticular Infertility & Pregnancy Loss Panel: What It Screens and the Evidence Behind It

articles.summary: A karyotype reads the shape and number of your chromosomes. A reproductive gene panel reads individual genes. They answer different questions after pregnancy loss — here is how they differ and why they work together.
articles.title: Karyotype vs. Reproductive Gene Panel: What Each One Can Tell You
